native_payload.intent: Fix a race in grpc-go addrConn where two concurrent connect() calls could both see Idle and start parallel connection attempts (orphaned transport). Callers of resetTransport now hold ac.mu across the call, and it is renamed resetTransportAndUnlock, which releases it. Must not introduce deadlocks, double-unlocks or lost state transitions.
residual_risks: updateAddrs' deferred ac.transport.GracefulClose() now runs while ac.mu is still held on behalf of the spawned resetTransportAndUnlock goroutine; GracefulClose -> onClose takes ac.mu and so waits for that goroutine to reach its Unlock. No cycle found (the goroutine's path to Unlock never takes the transport's lock and updateConnectivityState only schedules on the serializer); it would deadlock only if a user-supplied Backoff or minConnectTimeout callback blocked on the old transport. (adversarial)

resetTransportAndUnlock calls user-supplied ac.dopts.bs.Backoff and ac.dopts.minConnectTimeout with ac.mu held, as the old resetTransport did once it had locked; the lock is now held slightly longer on the connect()/updateAddrs paths. (adversarial)

Lock ownership is handed to a new goroutine in updateAddrs. Legal in Go, and updateAddrs touches no addrConn state after the go statement; every path in resetTransportAndUnlock (context-cancelled early return and the Connecting transition) unlocks exactly once.
testing_gaps: No regression test in the diff exercises concurrent connect() calls, or connect() racing updateAddrs, to assert that only one connection attempt starts. The race shows up only through dial counts or a test hook. The originating flaky test is the only coverage.
test/goaway_test.go and test/end2end_test.go match log strings naming the old 'resetTransport'. These did not match the current log text before this diff, so the rename does not cause it.

coverage.notes: Focused path: one independent adversarial read by a local adversarial reviewer on the same model family (cross-model peer unavailable in this configuration, so it is corroboration and not cross-model), plus this context's correctness read. No other reviewers and no validator ran. No CODING_STANDARDS.md, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md governs clientconn.go. No plan document found (requirements_completeness null). Learnings, agent-native gaps and deployment notes not assessed. Tests were not run. Lock discipline was checked by reading: connect() holds ac.mu after the Idle check, and resetTransportAndUnlock moves the state to Connecting before Unlock, so the check-and-set is atomic and the race window is closed; updateAddrs hands off the lock to the goroutine.
